text:
Idea: internal blog post arguing for trunk-based dev adoption. Mode develop, depth quick — got both, no setup turn needed.

State idea in one/two sentences, like convincing skeptical friend?

Two-week-old feature branches keep causing pain — merges turn into archaeology, integration bugs surface late. We should move to trunk-based dev: small commits straight to main, feature flags instead of long branches, catch problems next-day not next-month.

Restating: two-week feature branches cause late-surfacing merge/integration pain. Fix: trunk-based dev — small commits to main, feature flags replace long branches, catch problems next-day not next-month. Right?

Quick note: keep running draft saved as we go, in case session interrupts — only final brief at end counts as verdict.

Round 1 (a few tied questions): Who's post for — just your team, or org-wide, and do you have decision power to actually flip the switch, or just persuading? When you say "small commits straight to main," what's concrete workflow difference from now — same PR review, just merged same-day instead of after two weeks? And feature flags — got tooling for that already, or new investment needed?

Org-wide post, all ~80 engineers. Persuading only — no authority to flip switch, that's eng leadership call, but strong signal if post lands well. PR review stays same, just merge cadence changes: small commits straight to main daily/near-daily instead of sitting two weeks then one big merge. Feature flags — no tooling yet, that's new investment, biggest open question honestly.

Round 2 (last one, quick budget): Post's gonna touch feature-flag gap honestly, or lean past it? What's plan for that section — propose eng leadership invest in tooling too, or just flag it as open? Separately, what's evidence trunk-based fixes root cause here vs. just branch hygiene/discipline problem — seen it work elsewhere, or more instinct? And how'd a skeptic who likes long branches push back — what's strongest counter you want to preempt in post?

Post touch flag gap honest — not leaning past it. Section: flag it as open question, maybe suggest eng leadership evaluate tooling options, but not my call to spec solution in blog post. Evidence — mostly instinct plus two incidents, no hard "seen elsewhere" case study, don't wanna overclaim. Skeptic pushback: QA fears losing release branches — no stable branch to cut release from, no gate before prod. Preempt with: feature flags give same control point, just runtime not branch — decouple deploy from release.
